angle: event definition: stroke onset versus ball contact as time zero
study_sentence: Within-recording re-analysis of 12 putting recordings of 4 novices in which the event that defines time zero (stroke onset or ball contact, both located in a synchronised video) is the factor and the hit-minus-miss contrast of last-second band power is the outcome.
question: How does the hit-minus-miss contrast in pre-putt band power change when the same putts are time-locked to stroke onset instead of ball contact?

coverage.question: part
coverage.tested_part: whether the hit-minus-miss contrast in pre-putt band power changes when the same putts are time-locked to stroke onset instead of ball contact

untested.part: in which bands and regions, in which direction and by how much it changes

datasets: PilotDataV2 (CGX Quick-32r dry headset, one laboratory)
external_check.second_dataset: none: no second recording of putting or aiming with two movement events is on this machine; the public Carey et al. (2024) set has ball contact only and is not on disk
inventory: /Users/kyc/PythonProject/Golf: the study's own 12 keyed recordings with front video - the first data set
~/mne_data: cue-paced BCI and ERP sets - no self-paced aiming task with movement events
~/openneuro_data: ds003478, ds003775, ds003810, ds004148, ds004784, ds006801, ds007176, ds007222, ds007406, ds007558 - rest or cognitive tasks, no putting
OSF D6483 (careyetal2024): contact-locked only (backswing onset could not be detected), not on disk

claims.statement: Although movement-locked and contact-locked studies are compared as accounts of one preparation period, the hit-minus-miss contrast of band power in the last second differs between epochs time-locked to stroke onset and to ball contact for the same putts, which we conjecture is because the last second before ball contact contains the stroke.
reasons: the last second before ball contact contains the stroke, the last second before stroke onset does not
studies using the two locks report different outcome bands [cookeetal2014], [careyetal2024]

evidence.measure: T: per putt, band power (dB relative to the second -5 to -4 s before ball contact; putts with an onset-to-contact interval above 2 s dropped) in the last second of epochs time-locked to stroke onset and to ball contact, 12 ROI x band features -> hit-minus-miss median per recording -> median over recordings within participant -> median over participants, per lock -> difference between locks per feature -> maximum absolute difference over features
evidence.would_show: the time-zero definition alone changes the outcome contrast
evidence.refuted_if: T at or below the 95th percentile of its circular-shift null, or below 0.5 dB
evidence.can_fail: yes: the factor changes which second is analysed; if outcome is unrelated to band power in the interval between the two events the two contrasts agree and T stays inside the null

construction.predictor_formula: time-zero definition of each putt's last-second window: stroke onset or ball contact, both taken from the front video
construction.outcome_formula: T = max over 12 features of | hit-minus-miss contrast under the onset lock - hit-minus-miss contrast under the contact lock |, in dB
construction.computable_without_experiment: no: when the onset-to-contact interval is zero for every putt T is exactly 0, but for real intervals T depends on how band power between the two events differs by outcome, which no existing table gives
construction.free_quantity: the outcome dependence of band power during the interval between stroke onset and ball contact

claims.warrant: When the same trials give different contrasts under two event definitions, then results obtained under one definition cannot be compared with results under the other without correction

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that the lock alone can change the outcome contrast, so movement-locked and contact-locked studies describe different moments
outcomes.if_not: we learn that in these recordings the contrast does not depend on the lock, so the published disagreement needs another explanation (reference, baseline, sample)

negation.text: The hit-minus-miss contrast is the same under both locks

expected_direction.basis: contested: cookeetal2014 and careyetal2024 report different bands under different locks, but they also differ in reference, baseline and sample, and gallicchioring2018 treat one lock as sufficient

claims.smallest_effect_of_interest: 0.5 dB (design choice; the nearest reported outcome difference is 0.484 dB in careyetal2024)
claims.falsifier: E2: T is at or below the 95th percentile of its circular-shift null, or below 0.5 dB

rivals.how: stroke-onset detection errs differently for hit and miss putts (hesitant strokes), so onset-locked windows of the two classes cover different phases

rivals.ruled_out_by: E2 circular-shift null on the maximum

rivals.how: the contact-locked window contains movement artifact that the onset-locked window lacks, so the contrast differs for a non-neural reason
putts without a detectable onset are dropped, possibly more often in one outcome class
rivals.ruled_out_by: E1 reports drops by outcome and E2 excludes recordings whose drop share differs by more than 10 percentage points between outcomes

controls.negative: E5: the same statistic on the second from 2 to 1 s before each event, before the stroke under both locks and clear of the baseline second, with onsets from both detectors (E4); expected T inside its null
controls.negative_can_move: yes: the far window is cut from the same epochs by the same onset times, so outcome-dependent onset errors would shift it and move T
controls.positive: E6: +1 dB and +0.5 dB planted in frontal alpha (fixed in advance) of the onset-locked window of hit putts
controls.positive_expected: T takes an absolute value, so the planted 1 dB returns as |d0 + 1| - |d0|, which equals 1 dB only when the unplanted difference d0 of that feature is not negative; the feature is fixed in advance (frontal alpha) and d0 and its sign are reported; the control passes when T exceeds its null and 0.5 dB for the 1 dB plant, and the 0.5 dB plant shows whether an effect of the floor's size is detectable

scope.internal: in these 12 recordings the contrast does or does not depend on the lock
scope.external: shows whether the lock can matter in putting with a dry headset; does not explain the disagreement between published studies, whose data are not available here
limits: T takes an absolute value because the claim is unsigned: it asserts that the contrasts differ, not in which direction
the because-clause is a conjecture: no experiment separates the stroke from other events in the interval
stroke onset is detected from 30 fps video and from the head accelerometer, not from a putter sensor
4 participants: a permutation statement about these recordings

power.min_detectable: paired d >= 1.24 at 80% power, one-sided alpha = 0.05 (n = 4; worse in truth)

claims.statement: Although outcome contrasts are attributed to preparation, the interval from stroke onset to ball contact separates hit from miss putts within a recording.
reasons: stroke timing varies with distance and skill [diasetal2014], [wuetal2020]

evidence.measure: per recording AUC of the onset-to-contact interval for hit vs miss, minus 0.5 -> median over recordings within participant -> median over participants; two-sided
evidence.refuted_if: the hierarchical |AUC - 0.5| inside the circular-shift null
evidence.can_fail: yes: duration may be unrelated to outcome

claims.warrant: When a behavioural interval differs by outcome, windows locked to its two ends differ systematically by outcome

outcomes.if_supported: stroke duration is itself an outcome correlate and a reason for lock dependence
outcomes.if_not: stroke duration does not differ by outcome here, so lock dependence would have to come from the content of the interval

negation.text: Stroke duration is the same for hit and miss putts

expected_direction.basis: unknown: no source in the shortlist reports stroke duration by putt outcome

claims.falsifier: E7: hierarchical |AUC - 0.5| inside the circular-shift null

limits: absolute value because the claim is unsigned

power.min_detectable: paired d >= 1.24 at 80% power, one-sided alpha = 0.05 (n = 4; worse in truth)

claims.statement: The hit-minus-miss contrast of 36 window band power features is estimated under three locks (experimenter's P key, stroke onset, ball contact), each with a bootstrap interval over recordings.
reasons: a map lets readers see where the locks agree

evidence.measure: contrast per feature and lock, bootstrap 95% interval over recordings
evidence.would_show: which features depend on the lock

claims.warrant: A contrast with its interval describes the data

outcomes.if_supported: a table of contrasts under three locks
outcomes.if_not: intervals too wide to compare locks

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: a map of contrasts; no ordering asserted
claims.precision_target: bootstrap 95% interval over 12 recordings; aim: half-width at most 0.5 dB; the width obtained is reported

claims.statement: The distributions of the experimenter's P key minus ball contact and of stroke onset minus ball contact are estimated per recording and by outcome.
reasons: the size of the timing differences bounds how far the locks can differ

evidence.measure: median and inter-quartile range of each interval per recording and outcome; agreement between video and accelerometer onsets
evidence.would_show: how far apart the events are and how reliably onset is found

claims.warrant: Intervals between events are measured from their time stamps

outcomes.if_not: onset cannot be located reliably, which limits C1

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: the quantity has no direction to test
claims.precision_target: video resolution 33 ms per frame; aim: detector agreement within 100 ms for 80% of putts; the share obtained is reported

sample.target: putting studies that lock EEG to a movement event
sample.accessible: 12 recordings of 4 novices, dry headset, carpet target

predictor.phenomenon: the moment a study calls time zero
predictor.variable: stroke onset and ball contact from 30 fps video; onset also from accelerometer jerk
predictor.accuracy: contact audited against the accelerometer; onset has no physical reference
predictor.validity: criterion: the events correspond to the infrared (backswing) and piezo (impact) events of gallicchioring2018

outcome.variable: hit-minus-miss contrast of last-second band power
outcome.validity: face: the contrast the cited studies report

tradeoffs.change: no claim that the lock explains the disagreement between the two published studies
tradeoffs.because: their data are not on this machine
tradeoffs.lost: a direct resolution of that disagreement
tradeoffs.why: the gap is that the same putts were never analysed under both locks, which E2 does

tradeoffs.change: baseline moved to -5 to -4 s before ball contact; putts with an interval above 2 s dropped; recordings with unequal onset loss excluded; far-window control moved to 2 to 1 s before each event; E3 given a classification rule; E6 plants 0.5 and 1 dB in a pre-fixed feature; E9 added
tradeoffs.lost: putts with very long strokes and recordings with unequal onset loss no longer enter the primary test
tradeoffs.why: the same comparison with windows that cannot overlap the baseline

reader_doubts.doubt: 1. A difference between locks may be movement artifact in the contact-locked window, not brain activity
reader_doubts.how: E9 added: E2 repeated after regressing each feature on head acceleration of the same window; the confounding rival of C1 now points to E9

reader_doubts.doubt: 2. Four participants: failing to exceed the null says little and a pass concerns these recordings only
reader_doubts.how: data: only 4 participants with keyed recordings exist on this machine

reader_doubts.doubt: 3. The question asks how the contrast changes but the only rule is an unsigned maximum; which band, region and direction are only described
reader_doubts.how: coverage declared as part: the test covers whether the contrast changes; which bands and regions and in which direction is estimated by C3; Title and Short Hypothesis say so

reader_doubts.doubt: 4a. Putts without a detectable onset may be lost unequally by outcome and there is no rule
reader_doubts.how: E2 now excludes a recording when the share of dropped putts differs by more than 10 percentage points between hit and miss, and E1 reports it

reader_doubts.doubt: 4b. Event timing has no physical reference; two detectors may share an error
reader_doubts.how: data: the recordings hold no putter or impact sensor; the trigger channel is constant in every file

reader_doubts.doubt: 5. The far-window control coincides with the baseline second, and the onset-locked window can overlap the baseline
reader_doubts.how: E2 and E5 changed: the baseline is now the second -5 to -4 s before ball contact, the control window is 2 to 1 s before each event, and putts with an onset-to-contact interval above 2 s are dropped and counted

reader_doubts.doubt: 6. If stroke duration differs by outcome the reading of E2 is complicated and no rule combines E7 and E2
reader_doubts.how: E7 now states how the two are read together with E3

reader_doubts.doubt: 7. E3 has no pass/fail rule so the conjectured reason stays untested
reader_doubts.how: E3 now carries a classification rule (pseudo-onset T at least 0.8 of T: position of the window; below: putt-specific timing)

reader_doubts.doubt: 8. The 0.5 dB threshold comes from a different quantity and the positive control plants 1 dB in a feature chosen after looking
reader_doubts.how: E6 now plants both 1 dB and 0.5 dB in a feature fixed in advance (frontal alpha) and states the sign condition

reader_doubts.doubt: 9. One unpublished data set, no second data set
reader_doubts.how: data: no second recording with both movement events is on this machine; the Carey et al. set has ball contact only

reader_doubts.doubt: 10. C2, C3 and C4 are not stated in words
reader_doubts.how: each experiment entry now states the claim it serves
